text: A cement-plant maintenance workshop must re-machine a worn 80 mm drive shaft for a rotary kiln auxiliary fan. The tender specification (CPS) demands an h6 journal tolerance, a surface finish of Ra 0.8, and replacement of a keyway that has fretted after repeated start-stop cycles. The shaft transmits a steady torque through a single key, and previous failures showed fatigue cracks initiating at the keyway root. Plant engineers want to know whether the replacement shaft diameter keeps the torsional shear stress within the allowable limit for the specified alloy steel, given the motor rating and speed stated in the specification, before ordering the blank.

A fertiliser site needs a replacement thin-walled cylindrical storage vessel for an aqueous solution. The tender requires a corrosion allowance on top of the calculated wall thickness, welded longitudinal and circumferential seams with a stated joint efficiency, and a hydrotest at 1.3 times design pressure. The previous vessel thinned locally at a weld toe and was withdrawn from service. The designer must size the minimum wall thickness from the internal design pressure, inside radius, allowable stress and joint efficiency given in the specification.

A food-processing plant in the Meknès region is replacing a long steel process-water line between a ground tank and a header. The specification fixes the pipe inside diameter, the total developed length, the design flow rate and a Darcy friction factor taken from the roughness of aged commercial steel. Operations reports that the old line starved downstream users after scale build-up. The engineer must estimate the friction head loss along the line at the design flow before selecting the replacement pump.

A dairy plant relies on a plate-type heat exchanger to cool process fluid with chilled water. After fouling, the duty fell short of the specification. The maintenance tender requests cleaning, regasketing and a performance re-test against the guaranteed duty. The reliability engineer wants to confirm the heat transfer rate using the overall heat transfer coefficient, effective area and log-mean temperature difference stated in the datasheet, to decide whether cleaning alone restores the guaranteed duty.

A quarry operator found a surface crack in the welded boom of a loader. The maintenance tender asks for a fracture assessment before authorising repair welding. The plate is loaded in tension, the crack is a single edge flaw of measured depth, and the material datasheet gives a plane-strain fracture toughness. The engineer needs the stress at which the crack would reach critical size, using the geometry factor and toughness quoted in the report.

A logistics hub in Tanger is extending a steel mezzanine. The specification for the new pin-ended steel columns gives the section's second moment of area, the elastic modulus and the unsupported height. Several older columns showed lateral deflection under stacked pallet loads. The structural engineer must check the elastic critical buckling load of one pin-ended column from the specification data before accepting the supplier's section.

A pumping station is replacing a worn motor feeder and soft starter. The tender lists a three-phase supply, a motor rated by line voltage, line current and power factor, and requires a power audit after commissioning. The site electrician needs the real power drawn by the motor from the nameplate voltage, current and power factor to size the upstream protection and verify the energy audit figure.

A regional MRO shop is repairing a light-aircraft wing spar fitting that bent during a hard landing. The repair scheme replaces the fitting with a cantilevered lug whose tip deflection under the proof load must remain within the manufacturer's limit. The structures engineer needs the tip deflection from the proof load, lug length, elastic modulus and second moment of area given in the repair manual.
